title: Symmetric and asymmetric cryptography: where each one fits

videos.script: Two jobs hide under the word encryption. Keeping a message secret from whoever carries it. And agreeing on a secret with somebody you have never met. {{jobs}} Symmetric cryptography does the first, fast, with one shared key. You will encrypt a file, then watch authenticated encryption refuse a message with one bit changed. {{aead}} Asymmetric cryptography does the second. Two machines exchange only public keys, and each computes the same secret. {{agree}} Then a stopwatch. The fast half and the slow half, measured on the same laptop. {{speed}} Last, both halves at work: a WireGuard tunnel between the head office and the branch, and what the internet in between can still see. {{vpn}}
